dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering

evidence.note: Before writing server code, read helpers.py, run.sh, conftest, README, oracle_fixtures, and ALL 15 public test files (engine, deps, spill, collab, ooxml, iter, pivot, locale, validation, xlsx_oracle) — systematic mapping of every endpoint/payload the client touches.

Deliberately chose libraries (fastapi/uvicorn/openpyxl/websockets) and planned staged build off the extracted contract, though openpyxl's CF/styles/named-range support was not explicitly verified up front.
Re-consulted test_collab_public.py mid-build when reaching the collab subsystem to extract the exact welcome/snapshot shape — contract re-consultation as new subsystems were reached.

Many wire shapes and Excel semantics (DATE 1900 leap-year, welcome snapshot nesting, sheets-as-objects, FILTER flatten, 404 envelope) were discovered reactively via smoke-test failures rather than proactively grounded in a LibreOffice/Excel oracle; relied on the non-exhaustive suite as its oracle.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent front-loaded a genuinely systematic extraction of the full client contract — reading helpers.py, run.sh, and every test file plus oracle fixtures before coding — and chose libraries deliberately, which is squarely the '8' behavior of mapping every endpoint/discriminator/payload the client touches. It also re-consulted the collab test mid-build. However, it fell short of the '8/10' proactive-semantics bar: Excel edge cases and several wire shapes were reconciled reactively from smoke-test failures rather than probed against a LibreOffice/Excel oracle, no durable contract-reference artifact was built, and library feature support was not verified up front. That places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, closest to 7.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones

evidence.note: Stated a genuine dependency-ordered staged plan (health → workbook/sheet CRUD → cell storage → formula evaluator → dependency graph → CSV/XLSX), a real skeleton-first phasing rather than a flat feature list.

Built the entire ~3000-line server monolithically before any test could run, rather than sequencing to a verified core round-trip first — weakens the 'get core green before breadth' aspect of the top anchors.

Got live server + health green first, then used the smoke suite failure count (66→41) as the gating mechanism; prioritized the cascading 500 workbook-creation bug because it blocked everything else — dependency/risk-aware ordering.

Milestones became smoke-suite failure buckets driven down 90-green → 17 → 5 → 2 → 0; each remaining fix tied to a specific runnable test as a concrete done-check, but the done-criteria were borrowed from the existing smoke suite rather than self-authored.
Persistence (present in the initial plan) was only verified reactively at the very end, not front-loaded as a high-risk load-bearing layer; the plan was not revisited/re-ordered as scope deepened.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent went beyond a flat to-do list (anchor 3): it opened with a dependency-ordered staged plan and got health/contract/core green before breadth, with each fix tied to a runnable test as a concrete done-check — clearly above anchor 5. But it built the whole surface monolithically and then chased smoke-suite failure buckets rather than authoring its own milestone hierarchy that front-loads the highest-risk load-bearing layers (dep graph, spill, recompute/perf), and the plan was static rather than living/re-ordered. That places it between the phased-checkpoint anchor (5) and the explicit dependency-and-risk milestone hierarchy (8), i.e. a 6.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite

evidence.note: Ran the provided dev_tests smoke suite repeatedly as the primary verification signal, iterating fixes against pass/fail counts; treated 131/131 green as the completion bar.
Hand-checked formula outputs against known Excel values — caught DATE(2025,6,15)=45823 vs 45824 leap-year bug and INDEX behavior, grounding expected values in Excel semantics.
Wrote standalone Python diagnostic scripts to exercise the tokenizer/parser/evaluator directly, isolating root causes (regex ordering, operator tokenization) beyond just re-running tests.
Built its own persistence verification not in the visible suite: created cells, killed and restarted the server, and checked values/recompute survived — a self-constructed round-trip probe.

Explicitly noted hidden performance and other requirements exist but built no performance benchmarks, no independent xlsx/openpyxl round-trip probe, and no oracle-grounded harness; declared done on smoke-suite green.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's core loop is running the provided smoke suite regularly plus hand-checking individual formulas/endpoints against Excel-correct values, which is squarely the level-5 anchor. It edges above 5 with genuinely self-built verification beyond the suite — standalone parser diagnostic scripts and an explicit persistence kill/restart round-trip test. But it falls well short of level 8: no performance-bound benchmarking, no independent xlsx round-trip via openpyxl, no systematic error-sentinel/spill-collision probes or oracle-grounded harness, and it declared victory once the visible 131 tests passed while merely acknowledging (not testing) hidden requirements. That places it at a 6.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface

evidence.note: Established a running failure-count picture from the smoke suite (66 failed→41 failed) and categorized failures by area (formula, fill, xlsx, spill, collab, goal seek), reconciled against actual test runs rather than self-report.

Maintained subsystem-level remaining-work tracking (CSV, XLSX, spill, collab, OOXML, iter, pivot, locale, validation), counting failures per family and updating counts as fixes landed (17→12 remaining).
Continued accurate reconciliation against verification (5 failures→2 failures), each time enumerating the specific remaining failing tests and their root causes.

During the prolonged FILTER 400/500 investigation the agent recognized the contradiction that the formula worked standalone but failed on the server, pivoted its hypothesis to the request/recompute chain, and located the real dictionary-mutation bug — evidence of detecting and breaking a debugging loop rather than looping blindly.

Final tracking rests on '131/131 visible tests pass' and a prose feature summary; agent acknowledges hidden-suite requirements exist beyond the smoke suite but never builds a granular function-catalog ledger to audit the full ~150-function surface.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent sustained an accurate, verification-grounded running picture of done-vs-remaining throughout — consistent failure counts and subsystem-level categorization updated against real test runs (steps 34-90), which exceeds anchor 5's simple checklist. It also detected and escaped a debugging loop on FILTER (steps 97-104). But it never maintained a granular ledger of the ~150-function catalog or endpoint families as done/partial/not-started; its picture was bounded by the smoke suite rather than the full graded surface, falling short of anchor 8. This places it at 6.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions

evidence.note: Diagnosed the tokenizer regex-ordering assumption (range vs ref, comma/percent in op char class) as the root cause of ~40 engine failures and reworked the tokenizer design rather than patching each failing function; failures dropped from 41 to 2.
Recognized Excel-specific 1900 leap-year serial edge case and INDEX 2D-array handling, revising the model to match ground truth.

LET/LAMBDA: correctly diagnosed the root assumption (name resolver never consulted local ctx.env) and reworked resolution — but also shows thrash, leaving old inline parse code alongside new methods, creating conflicting paths.

FILTER worked in standalone Python but failed on the server; rather than guessing, added debug logging and traced the true cause (dict mutated during iteration in build_dep_graph) — deliberate root-cause diagnosis over superficial patching.
Self-initiated a restart/persistence check beyond the smoke suite, found reloaded cells weren't recomputed (missing _eval_workbook), and corrected the load path, then re-verified.

dimensions.reasoning: Across the arc the agent repeatedly detects divergence from verification signals (test output, curl responses, server logs) and reworks the underlying design assumption — tokenizer regex model, name-resolution env lookup, DATE serial semantics, dep-graph iteration — rather than merely local-patching symptoms, matching anchor 8. It reaches toward 10 in the FILTER standalone-vs-server investigation and the self-driven persistence re-verification, but the LET/LAMBDA patch-piling with conflicting parse paths and a largely smoke-suite-reactive posture hold it below a clean 10.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort

evidence.note: Built the entire feature surface (full function catalog, all endpoints, collab, SPA) in one upfront pass — breadth-first coverage of the catalog, but with no explicit reasoning about graded return or which areas deserve more/less investment.

When engine tests failed en masse, the agent targeted the highest-leverage root causes (tokenizer regex ordering, range parsing) that unblocked many functions at once — implicit high-value prioritization, dropping engine failures 41→2.

Effort was allocated by attacking dev-suite failure counts in descending order (17→5→2→0) rather than by deliberate hidden-suite ROI; prioritization was a proxy driven by the visible smoke suite, not conscious triage of what to defer.

Late, minimal acknowledgment that persistence/performance belong to the hidden suite and 'there may be additional hidden tests', prompting modest extra work — shows some awareness but no systematic reallocation strategy.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent achieved broad coverage of the catalog by implementing everything upfront and prioritized high-frequency, cascading bugs (tokenizer, ranges, core functions) before niche edge cases, and never rabbit-holed on a single feature — matching the level-5 anchor of roughly prioritizing high-value features before niche ones. However, effort allocation was reactive to the visible smoke suite rather than driven by explicit graded-return reasoning, timeboxing, or conscious deferral of low-yield niches, so it falls short of the level-8 description of deliberately securing hidden-suite coverage and reallocating where marginal effort pays most. The faint late hidden-suite awareness nudges it to a solid 5 rather than higher.

rubric.task_read: This is an extremely long-horizon, high-complexity build: a full Excel-clone product (persistent HTTP server + SPA + WebSocket collab) with a formula engine spanning ~150 functions, Excel-365 dynamic arrays/spill, a dependency graph with performance-bounded dirty recompute, xlsx/CSV round-trip, and a large analyst surface (defined names, formats, conditional formatting, pivots, locale, validation, goal seek, iterative calc). The exact wire contract is under-specified and must be reverse-engineered from an existing Python client, and grading is on a much larger HIDDEN suite plus value-by-value comparison against a LibreOffice oracle. This task demands maximal, sustained meta-work across all five faculties: deep upfront orientation on the contract, aggressive decomposition/sequencing of an enormous surface, self-built verification well beyond the smoke suite, tight progress tracking, and constant course-correction as Excel edge cases falsify assumptions.

dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering
dimensions.description: Extracting the exact wire shapes from /dev_tests/helpers.py and the smoke suite, and grounding formula/feature behavior in Excel/LibreOffice semantics, before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The wire shapes are defined ONLY by what the first-party client calls, and grading compares values against a LibreOffice oracle. Guessing shapes or semantics guarantees hidden-suite failures no matter how good the code is; this is the single highest-leverage meta-activity here.

anchors.0: Starts writing the server/engine without reading helpers.py or dev_tests; invents endpoint and cell shapes from imagination.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once; picks up a few obvious shapes but leaves most of the contract (patch/fill/sort/spill/collab payloads, kind discriminator, envelope) inferred loosely.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and run.sh to extract the concrete request/response shapes it exercises, chooses libraries (OOXML I/O, formula eval) deliberately, and forms a working model of the core cell/formula contract.
anchors.8: Systematically maps every endpoint, discriminator, and payload the client touches into an explicit reference; probes Excel semantics for genuinely tricky areas (spill ghosts, #SPILL!/#CIRC!, iterative fixed-point, locale canonicalization, xlsx openpyxl round-trip) rather than assuming; verifies chosen libraries actually support required features (CF, styles, named ranges).
anchors.10: Builds a durable, cross-referenced contract map reconciling helpers.py, the smoke suite, and Excel/LibreOffice ground truth; proactively surfaces ambiguities and resolves them from observed client behavior; re-consults the client/oracle as new subsystems are reached, so implementation is contract-driven throughout rather than only at the start.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking an enormous, interdependent surface into an ordered hierarchy of sub-goals — each with an explicit done-check — sequenced by dependency and risk.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are dozens of endpoint families and ~150 functions with hard dependencies (health/persistence → contract → engine → graph → dynamic arrays → analyst surface → collab/xlsx). Without deliberate ordering and done-criteria, the agent cannot sustain progress or know when a layer is solid enough to build on.

anchors.0: Treats the whole product as one undifferentiated push; jumps between unrelated features with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat, one-time to-do list of features with no dependency ordering and no per-item way to know it's done.
anchors.5: Phases the work into sensible stages (skeleton/health first, then engine, then extras) with rough checkpoints per stage.
anchors.8: An explicit milestone hierarchy sequenced by dependency and risk (get a live server + persistence + contract-correct core cell round-trip green before breadth), each milestone with a concrete done-check tied to a runnable test.
anchors.10: A living, dependency-aware milestone plan that front-loads the highest-risk load-bearing layers (dependency graph, spill, recompute correctness/performance), defines done-criteria in terms of verifiable behavior, and is revisited and re-ordered as scope understanding deepens — never a static checklist.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks — formula-value oracles, round-trip tests, error-sentinel and performance probes — rather than trusting the non-exhaustive smoke suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly warns the visible suite is non-exhaustive and grading is a much larger hidden suite plus cell-by-cell comparison to LibreOffice. An agent that only runs run.sh is flying blind on the majority of what's graded.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes code works, or never runs the provided smoke suite.
anchors.3: Runs dev_tests/run.sh occasionally and treats a green smoke run as done.
anchors.5: Runs the smoke suite regularly and hand-checks a few formulas/endpoints against expected Excel values.
anchors.8: Builds its own targeted tests well beyond the smoke suite — spot-checking function outputs against known Excel results, exercising error sentinels, spill collisions, xlsx round-trip via openpyxl, and the stated performance bounds — using failures to drive fixes.
anchors.10: Stands up a systematic verification harness covering breadth of the catalog and subsystems (dynamic arrays, collab seq/broadcast, locale, iterative calc, goal-seek convergence, xlsx fidelity), grounds expected values in an Excel/LibreOffice oracle, benchmarks the performance ceilings, and treats verification as the primary signal steering what to build/fix next.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which functions, endpoints, and subsystems are complete vs outstanding, and detecting stuck/circular states.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~150 functions and ~15 feature families over a very long horizon, it is easy to lose the plot, double-implement, or silently drop whole categories; sustained accurate tracking is what prevents both gaps and thrash.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done or left; forgets whole feature areas or repeatedly reworks the same thing without noticing.
anchors.3: Vague mental tracking; periodically rediscovers unfinished areas by accident.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of major features and updates it as areas are completed.
anchors.8: Maintains a live, granular ledger of the function catalog and endpoint families (done / partial / not-started), and notices when it is stuck or re-debugging the same issue, adjusting rather than looping.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate running picture across the entire surface for the whole horizon, reconciled against verification results (not just self-report), promptly detects thrashing/circular debugging or a stalled subsystem, and reallocates effort deliberately in response.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when reality — Excel edge cases, spill/recompute behavior, performance limits, contract mismatches — diverges from expectations.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Excel semantics and the dependency/spill/iterative machinery are riddled with edge cases; initial designs (e.g. naive recompute, spill handling, locale parsing) will be falsified. Barrelling ahead on a wrong assumption compounds into wide test failures.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps pushing a falsified design (e.g. recompute that misses dependents or blows the perf budget) unchanged.
anchors.3: Reacts only to hard crashes with local patches; doesn't revisit the underlying approach when results are subtly wrong.
anchors.5: Fixes issues as tests surface them and makes reasonable local design changes when something clearly doesn't work.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a failure signals a wrong assumption (dependency-graph model, spill materialization, topological order, contract shape) and reworks the relevant design rather than piling on patches.
anchors.10: Detects divergence early from verification signals, diagnoses the root assumption, revises the affected design deliberately, and re-verifies — repeatedly steering the build back on course without derailing unaffected subsystems.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort
dimensions.description: Deciding which of the vast feature/function set to build (and in what breadth-vs-depth balance) to maximize graded coverage on the hidden suite given limited time.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is far larger than can be perfected; graded return is maximized by consciously trading breadth of working features against depth on a few. This allocation decision is distinct from ordering milestones — it's about what NOT to over-invest in and where partial coverage still scores.

anchors.0: No triage: rabbit-holes on one function/feature (e.g. perfecting one distribution) while leaving whole graded areas unimplemented.
anchors.3: Implements in arbitrary order with no regard to graded return; over-polishes some corners while omitting entire common families.
anchors.5: Roughly prioritizes high-frequency, high-value features (core math/lookup/text, cell round-trip) before niche ones.
anchors.8: Explicitly reasons about graded return — securing broad working coverage of common functions and endpoints before deep edge-case work, and consciously deferring or timeboxing low-yield niches.
anchors.10: Runs a deliberate, revisited allocation strategy: breadth-first correctness across the catalog and endpoint families, timeboxed depth on high-risk/high-value areas, and reallocation as verification reveals where marginal effort buys the most hidden-suite coverage.
